items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: Simple workflows take a few days. Larger systems, like dashboards or platforms, take two to six weeks.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. I build it, explain it in plain English, and leave you with notes you can follow.

projects.title: Instagram analytics dashboard
projects.summary: Instagram numbers pulled automatically into a dashboard with charts, month-over-month changes and AI-written recommendations.
projects.problem: Monthly social reports meant exporting numbers by hand, rebuilding the same charts, and guessing what to post next.
projects.solution: A connection to the Meta Graph API that pulls account and post data straight into a Google Sheets and Excel dashboard, compares each month to the last, and adds AI-generated recommendations.

steps.label: Meta Graph API
steps.detail: Pulls account and post insights from a creator account linked to a Facebook Page.

steps.label: Clean and organise
steps.detail: Formats the raw numbers into tidy monthly tables.

steps.label: Charts
steps.detail: Builds reach, engagement and growth charts automatically.

steps.label: Month over month
steps.detail: Highlights what went up, what dropped and by how much.

steps.label: AI recommendations
steps.detail: Writes plain-English suggestions for next month's content.

results: Reports ready the moment the month ends

projects.title: Bank transaction tracker
projects.summary: Every bank credit alert is read, logged into a Google Sheet and announced, without anyone opening their inbox.
projects.problem: Confirming payments meant scrolling through bank alert emails and typing sender names and amounts into a sheet.
projects.solution: An n8n workflow that watches for bank credit-alert emails, extracts the sender, amount and description, logs each payment as a new row, and sends a notification.

steps.label: Gmail trigger
steps.detail: Fires the moment a bank credit alert lands.

steps.label: Read the alert
steps.detail: Extracts sender name, amount and description from the email.

steps.label: Sheets: add row
steps.detail: Logs the payment with date and details.

steps.label: Notify
steps.detail: Sends an alert so the team knows money came in.

results: A running record that's always up to date

projects.title: DocuSend
projects.summary: Contract-of-sale documents for a real estate company, filled from a form and emailed to the client once payment is confirmed.
projects.problem: Each contract of sale was typed up by hand: client name, date, amount paid and property, with room for costly mistakes.
projects.solution: A form feeds the client details into a contract template, generates the finished document and emails it to the client as soon as payment is complete.

steps.label: Form submitted
steps.detail: Client name, property, date and amount paid are captured once.

steps.label: Fill the template
steps.detail: Details are placed into the contract of sale automatically.

steps.label: Payment check
steps.detail: The document waits until payment is confirmed.

steps.label: Email the client
steps.detail: The finished contract is sent straight to the client.

results: Fewer errors in names and amounts

projects.title: Landnest rentals platform
projects.summary: An estate management platform where property owners list rentals and people apply to become tenants.
projects.problem: Rental listings and tenant applications were scattered across calls, chats and paper forms.
projects.solution: One platform where owners post rental listings, people browse and apply to become tenants, and the team reviews every application in one place.

steps.label: List a property
steps.detail: Owners post rentals with photos, price and details.

steps.label: Browse
steps.detail: Prospective tenants search and compare listings.

steps.label: Apply
steps.detail: Applicants submit their details through one simple form.

steps.label: Review
steps.detail: The team reviews applications and updates their status.

results: Listings and applications in one place
A clear record for every property
